title: General structured data guidelines
measures: Rules for rich-result eligibility: JSON-LD recommended; do not mark up content not visible to readers; do not mark up misleading content such as fake reviews; structured data must be a true representation of page content; use the most specific applicable type; structured-data issues can lead to a manual action that removes rich-result eligibility; correct markup does not ensure a rich result appears.
limitations: Applies to Google Search rich results; other consumers of schema.org markup may behave differently. Page 'last updated' date as shown on retrieval.

title: Review snippet (Review, AggregateRating) structured data
measures: Self-serving review guideline: if the entity being reviewed controls the reviews about itself, its pages using LocalBusiness or Organization structured data are ineligible for the star review feature, including reviews shown via embedded third-party widgets.
limitations: Covers eligibility for Google's review rich result only.

title: Latest Google Search documentation updates
measures: Changelog. May 8, 2026: deprecation notice added for the FAQ rich result, which 'will no longer appear in Google Search starting May 7, 2026'. June 2026: FAQ rich result documentation removed because the feature is no longer shown. The former FAQPage documentation URL now redirects to this changelog.
limitations: Changelog summaries; read the linked documentation for detail. Google may change features again.

title: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search
measures: Google's guidance that optimizing for generative AI search is still SEO; features use retrieval-augmented generation and query fan-out; structured data is not required for generative AI search and there is no special schema; Business Profile details can help local visibility in AI responses; seeking inauthentic mentions is not helpful; points to the Search Console Generative AI performance report; warns no third-party tool has access to internal ranking or AI systems.
limitations: Covers Google Search only, not ChatGPT, Copilot, Perplexity or other assistants.

title: Generative AI performance report (Search)
dataYear: Rolled out to all websites as of 2026-08-31 per the page
measures: Impressions of links to a site in AI Overviews and AI Mode, by page, country, date and device; data comes from the Web search type of the Performance report; excludes Search Labs experiments; usual 1,000-row and aggregation limits apply.
limitations: Reports impressions only per the documentation retrieved; does not show what the AI response said or whether the site was recommended.

title: Search generative AI control
dataYear: Rolled out to all websites as of 2026-08-31 per the page
measures: Search Console setting to include (default) or exclude a site's links and content from AI Overviews, AI Mode and generative AI features in Discover; exclusion removes impressions and traffic from those features and use of the site's content as grounding input.
limitations: Does not affect AI training (Google-Extended governs that) or other parts of Search.

title: [GA4] Default channel group
measures: Defines the AI Assistant channel: users arriving from sources like ChatGPT, Gemini, Deepseek, Copilot or Grok, excluding Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode; medium set to 'ai-assistant' when the referrer matches Google's list of AI assistants, or when the medium exactly matches 'ai-assistant'.
limitations: Google maintains the referrer list; visits without a referrer or tag fall into other channels such as Direct.

title: Person
measures: Vocabulary for individuals, including jobTitle, worksFor, hasCredential, alumniOf, memberOf and knowsAbout.
limitations: Vocabulary definition; does not describe how any search engine uses the properties.

title: IndividualPhysician
measures: Defines IndividualPhysician as 'an individual medical practitioner' with practicesAt pointing to a MedicalOrganization; Physician is defined as an individual physician or a physician's office.
limitations: Schema.org does not define a dentist-specific person type; whether a dentist should be typed this way is a judgement call. Google documents no rich result for it.

title: Trade Regulation Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials (final rule)
measures: Publication record of the FTC's final rule, 89 FR 68034, effective 2024-10-21.
limitations: Metadata retrieved via the Federal Register API; the operative text is cited from eCFR (16 CFR Part 465). ftc.gov could not be retrieved on 2026-11-08.

title: 47 CFR 64.1200 — Delivery restrictions (TCPA rules)
dataYear: eCFR current text on retrieval, noting a pending amendment published at 91 FR 67219 (2026-10-26)
measures: Consent requirements for autodialed or prerecorded calls and texts to wireless numbers; health care message provisions referencing HIPAA covered entities; (a)(10) revocation of consent by any reasonable method, with 'stop', 'quit', 'end', 'revoke', 'opt out', 'cancel' or 'unsubscribe' replies treated as revocation.
limitations: Federal rule text only; whether a review-request text is telemarketing, informational or a health care message is a legal question for counsel. State texting laws are not covered.

title: Enhancing the Ability of Consumers To Control the Robocalls (final rule)
measures: FCC rule, 91 FR 67214, effective 2026-11-25: callers may treat a revocation as applying only to the category of informational robocalls it was directed at, and may designate an exclusive means to revoke consent. A companion proposed rule (91 FR 67239) seeks comment on further changes.
limitations: Abstract reviewed via the Federal Register API; full rule text not analysed here. Requirements change; confirm with counsel.

title: 45 CFR 164.502 — Uses and disclosures of protected health information: general rules
measures: HIPAA Privacy Rule general standard: a covered entity or business associate may not use or disclose protected health information except as permitted or required by the rule.
limitations: Rule text; application to a specific reply is a question for the practice's privacy officer or counsel.

title: Report inappropriate reviews on your Business Profile
measures: Only reviews that violate Google policies are eligible for removal; do not report a review because you disagree with it; Google does not get involved in disputes between businesses and customers; evaluation typically takes several days; status is tracked in the Reviews Management Tool; a separate route exists for extortion scams involving negative reviews.
limitations: Process may change; outcomes are decided by Google.

title: Manage customer reviews
measures: Replying requires a verified profile; replies are checked against content policies (usually up to 10 minutes, sometimes up to 30 days); replies are public and appear as the business; the reviewer is notified and can still change the review.

title: Disclosing Patient Information in Responses to Online Reviews: Recent OCR Enforcement Action Is a Cautionary Tale
measures: Law-firm summary of HHS OCR's $50,000 civil money penalty (announced March 2022) against a North Carolina dental practice whose Google reply disclosed a patient's full name and visit details; a 2019 $10,000 dental settlement over Yelp replies; and a 2013 OCR letter stating a covered entity 'may not confirm or deny that a particular person was, in fact, a patient'.
limitations: Secondary source. hhs.gov blocked automated retrieval on 2026-11-08, so the underlying OCR documents were not checked directly.

title: HIPAA-regulated entities must use caution responding to online reviews
measures: Law-firm summary of OCR actions on review replies: a June 2023 psychiatric-practice settlement; a December 2022 California dental practice settlement of $23,000 plus a two-year corrective action plan over Yelp replies that added full names, visit and insurance details; earlier dental actions of $50,000 (2022) and $10,000 (2019).
limitations: Secondary source; primary HHS documents not retrieved (hhs.gov blocked automated access on 2026-11-08).

title: Dental Practice Fined $10,000 for PHI Disclosures on Yelp
measures: Trade-press summary of the 2019 OCR settlement with a Dallas dental practice: Yelp reply disclosed a patient's last name, condition, treatment plan, insurance and cost; further disclosures found on the review page; missing social-media PHI policies; $10,000 and a corrective action plan with no admission of liability.
limitations: Secondary source; primary HHS resolution agreement not retrieved.
